basic_pitch_tf.why: Basic Pitch's training objective and optimizer are Keras 2 code (basic_pitch.models.loss, basic_pitch.train), so its training oracle needs TensorFlow. basic-pitch 0.4.0's `tf` extra pins tensorflow-macos below 2.15.1 on Darwin, and TensorFlow 2.16 moved to Keras 3, so 2.15.0 is the newest version that runs the reference's own code. TensorFlow 2.15 needs numpy below 2, which is why this interpreter is separate from basic_pitch's: the inference and GTCRN records there were measured on numpy 2.0.2. In a fresh session `models.model()` builds exactly the released SavedModel's 24 variables by name and shape, 16,864 values of which 16,782 train; the 35,736 the ONNX graph holds adds the constant-Q tensors, which Keras computes at run time and does not store. basic_pitch_training copies the SavedModel's variables into it by position. `basic_pitch_targets` reads mirdata (1.0.0 here), the library `basic_pitch.data` builds its training targets with, installed under a constraint that holds numpy, TensorFlow, and torch.

allin1.why: All-In-One needs madmom (unmaintained, installed from git and compiled with Cython) beside a current torch, which no other oracle wants. NATTEN is installed too, but only as a CHECK: 0.21 dropped the biased 1D/2D kernels the released model imports, so the oracle substitutes a torch neighborhood attention transcribed from NATTEN 0.14.6's own index rules and verifies its neighbor selection against the installed kernel (through the flex backend, at a power-of-two head dimension) before recording anything. The model sources are vendored rather than pip-installed, at IK_ALLIN1_SRC, because the package pulls hydra and demucs at import.

deepseek_v41.why: transformers carries deepseek_v4 and no deepseek_v41, so the reference is the release's own inference/model.py. It needs nothing beyond torch; this interpreter is already provisioned.
deepseek_v41.source: ~/.inferkit-validation/reference-sources/deepseek-v41 (IK_DEEPSEEK_V41_SRC): model.py, engram.py, vision.py, image_processor.py and convert.py from the release's inference/ directory, fetched rather than cloned.
deepseek_v41.note: model.py imports six symbols from kernel, whose real bodies are tilelang kernels that compile for CUDA. The mode stands a CPU kernel module in front of it: the two quantized GEMMs raise (only a quantized weight reaches them, and a float configuration has none), the two activation quantizers are neutral (inplace=True is a fused quantize-then-dequantize, so skipping it gives the unquantized model), and sparse_attn and hc_split_sinkhorn are transcribed from transformers' own plain-PyTorch deepseek_v4, the third party this package already measured those two mechanisms against. kernel.py itself is never imported, so tilelang is not needed. The vision mode needs no substitute at all: vision.py imports torch and nothing else, and the released tower ships unquantized.
deepseek_v41.decode_note: deepseek_v41_decode records a prefill of 11 tokens then three single-token steps, with every buffer a step carries written out after each: the sliding window, the shared compressed key-value, the index keys, the compressor's parked partial group and the n-gram id history. The prompt is 11 on purpose. It is odd, so a ratio-2 group parks a partial at the boundary; longer than the window of 8, so the ring has already wrapped; and longer than the n-gram look-back, so that look-back crosses the prefill/decode split. ONE LINE OF THE REFERENCE IS CORRECTED: Indexer.forward publishes shared_attn.index_k only when its compressor emitted a latent, while _compress_kv publishes unconditionally, so on a no-emit step a ratio-2 layer scores against whatever layer published last, at a different stride. The publish is hoisted BEFORE the call, because Indexer.forward reads index_k itself and publishing on the way out leaves the owner scoring its own step against stale keys.
deepseek_v41.quantized_note: deepseek_v41_quantized and deepseek_v41_dspark_quantized run the same code with the kernel shim's act_quant and fp4_act_quant made REAL, transcribed from kernel.py: the next power of two of the block maximum times the reciprocal of the format's range, clamp, cast, cast back, multiply; the compressed latent alone divides by 6 and rounds that scale to e4m3. They run under the gemma environment, not this one, because the fp4 cast needs ml_dtypes, which this interpreter does not carry. The index heads are 32 wide in both, because the real kernel asserts a row divides into its fp4 blocks. The unquantized records reproduce byte for byte with the switch in place.
deepseek_v41.bf16_note: deepseek_v41_bf16_plain builds the release's code under set_dtype(bfloat16), so every parameter the constructor does not make float32 is bf16 and every activation is bf16 between the places the code computes in float32; deepseek_v41_bf16 does the same with the quantizers and the narrow GEMMs of deepseek_v41_quantized. Both run under the gemma environment for ml_dtypes, and both record dtype::<parameter> (1 for float32) from the reference's own state_dict, which is what the port's float32 rule is held to. Every deepseek_v41 record also carries probe.hc.*: hc_post and hc_pre on independently drawn copies from a private generator, because the decoder's own copies never diverge far enough to tell which index comb sums over. Adding it left every other entry byte-identical. The decode, dspark, vision and vl_router modes each have a _bf16 twin built through the same helper, and each float32 record reproduces byte for byte with the switch in place. deepseek_v41_vision_bf16 runs under sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH), torch's definition of scaled_dot_product_attention, because the default CPU backend's bf16 attention exponentiates through its own fast polynomial; the default backend's result is kept as default_sdpa.* for comparison.
deepseek_v41.v4_note: The deepseek_v4_* modes run V4's own inference/model.py behind the same kernel shim: ~/.inferkit-validation/reference-sources/deepseek-v4 (V4 Flash, whose model.py V4 Pro shares) and deepseek-v4-pro-0813, each fetched from the release's inference/ directory at a recorded revision (SOURCE). V4's indexer rotates through fast_hadamard_transform, a CUDA library; the mode supplies it as the library's hadamard_transform_ref with the kernel's float32 accumulation and one rounding, and a float32 record runs the same rotation past rotate_activation's bf16 assertion. deepseek_v4_pro_dspark runs 0813's DSpark stack (two stages over the decoder's experts) through its own forward and forward_spec at temperature 0, and records each stage's sparse-attention inputs and output.
deepseek_v41.image_note: deepseek_v41_image measures the PREPROCESSOR, which deepseek_v41_vision leaves out by starting from patches. Its input is a deterministic RGB array encoded to PNG only so the release's own load_image runs its real path; PNG is lossless, so the recorded pixels are exactly the ones the reference resized and a port reads them without agreeing about PNG decoding. Two sizes are recorded: an ordinary picture whose sides are not multiples of the patch size, so the pad runs, and one wide enough to trip vision_max_wh_ratio, which takes the resize-without-padding branch. Matching it needs PIL's two-pass 8-bit resample in fixed point, not a float resample of the same coefficients.

SD3.5-large (8B) transformer. The official stabilityai repo is gated; this is an ungated mirror of the same geometry. The urllib stall this note used to describe was IPv6: huggingface.co advertises sixteen IPv6 addresses ahead of its IPv4 ones and Python tried each in turn, which shapes.py now avoids by ordering the IPv4 addresses first.
SD3.5-medium (2.5B, MMDiT-X) transformer, which exercises the dual-attention path (attn2 on the first thirteen layers). Ungated mirror.

FLUX.1 [schnell] (12B) transformer. Ungated mirror of the Apache release (the official black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell repo is gated). Used for the released-weight numeric parity too: provision the whole mirror to a directory, add the T5 spiece.model (from google/t5-v1_1-xxl, since FLUX's tokenizer_2 ships only tokenizer.json) into tokenizer_2/, and set IK_VAL_FLUX_SCHNELL (its transformer/ subdir) + IK_VAL_FLUX_SCHNELL_FULL (the directory). Records: run_reference.py flux_real (the 12B transformer's velocity on a tiny-spatial input, bf16, ~24 GB resident -> IK_PARITY_FLUX_REAL) and flux_text (the CLIP-L + T5-XXL text front end, ~10 GB -> IK_PARITY_FLUX_TEXT), both under the sd oracle (sdvenv: diffusers 0.31 + accelerate for the low-memory 24 GB load, plus protobuf + sentencepiece for the T5 tokenizer). The HF IPv6 stall (shapes.py's getaddrinfo IPv4-first patch) applies to the download.
FLUX.1 [dev] (12B) transformer, guidance-distilled (the guidance_embedder the schnell size lacks). The official BFL repo is gated; this is an ungated mirror.

The released Qwen4-Exp: 180B of bfloat16 across 131 shards, 1658 tensors, 360 GB. The decoder is 1163 of them; the rest are the vision tower, the multi-token-prediction head, the derived hash buffers, and the n-gram table's 128 shards.

The released DeepSeek V4.1 (MIT, 763B): 96085 tensors across 48 shards, 510 GB, quantized as shipped — int8 four-bit-packed routed experts, fp8 attention and n-gram tables, bf16 embeddings. 47006 tensors are the decoder, 46412 are block scales that decode one of them, and 2667 are the multi-token/DSpark heads, the vision tower, the aligner, and the image delimiters. Read by NFKMLXDeepSeekTests through IK_SHAPES_DEEPSEEK_V41 / IK_CONFIG_DEEPSEEK_V41 / IK_INDEX_DEEPSEEK_V41, which take shapes.py's shapes.json beside its dtypes.json as well as the combined format the earlier releases were captured in.

FLUX.2 [klein] 4B (3.88B) transformer, the FLUX.2 release that is NOT gated, so this inventory comes from Black Forest Labs' own repository rather than a mirror (169 tensors). FLUX.2 [dev] (32B) and FLUX.2 [klein] 9B are gated: accepting their license is a user action, so their headers cannot be walked here. The [dev] geometry is pinned instead by its published parameter total, which the declared configuration reproduces exactly (NFKMLXReleasedSizesTests.testFlux2DevParameterTotalMatchesTheRelease). The klein 9B total pins 32 heads, a 12288-wide text sequence and no guidance embedding, and leaves the split between double and single blocks open, because a double block costs exactly two single blocks; the split is read from the base-9B inventory below rather than chosen.

LTX-2.3 22B audio-video transformer (`LTX2VideoTransformer3DModel`, 4186 tensors across 8 shards, 19.0 GB bf16). Every LTX-2.5 repository is gated (`Lightricks/LTX-2.5`, `LTX-2.5-Diffusers`, `LTX-2.5-Pre-Trained`), and accepting a license is a user action, so the structural check runs against LTX-2.3, the same class at the arrangement its `config.json` declares (`rope_type` split, `cross_attn_mod` true, `use_prompt_embeddings` false). LTX-2.5's three declared differences — `ff_bias` false, `use_prompt_adaln_single` false, `use_keyframes_abs_pos_embedding` true — are measured numerically instead, by the `l25` half of `run_reference.py ltx2`. `Lightricks/LTX-2.3` itself ships a single-file checkpoint with no config, which is why the diffusers organization's conversion is the source here.

The base 9B RELEASE's transformer (17 GB, two shards, fetched with curl -4), under IK_VAL_FLUX2_KLEIN_BASE_9B. It backs `run_reference.py flux2_real` (the whole transformer at bfloat16, 18 GB) and `flux2_real_truncated` (the first two double and two single blocks at float32 and bfloat16, read tensor by tensor through safe_open so the release never exists whole in memory). The whole release is 36 GB at float32, which this machine cannot hold. Its VAE is byte-identical to klein 4B's (same lfs sha256), so that stage is covered by the klein 4B release. The 18 GB oracle is killed when it shares the machine with a build or another oracle; it ran cleanly with 82% of memory free.

FLUX.2 [klein] BASE 9B transformer (9.08B, 233 tensors across 2 shards). Gated, and the gate was accepted for THIS repository alone: `FLUX.2-klein-9B` itself, `FLUX.2-klein-9b-kv` and `FLUX.2-dev` still refuse a weight fetch. It is the inventory that resolves what the 9.08B parameter total could not, `num_layers` 8 against `num_single_layers` 24, because a double block costs exactly two single blocks and seventeen splits reach the same total. Its config's own `_name_or_path` is `/raid/yiyi/klein-9b-diffusers/transformer`, which is how one release's headers come to pin the other's geometry. Read by NFKMLXReleasedSizesTests.testFlux2Klein9BMatchesTheReleasedShapes through IK_SHAPES_ROOT.

FLUX.2 [klein] 9B KV transformer (233 tensors, 2 shards). Its config and every tensor's name and shape are the base 9B's; the release differs in being TRAINED for the reference cache, an inference mechanism in which reference tokens take the modulation of timestep 0, attend only to one another, and have their keys and values cached from the first step. Nothing in the release's files marks this: its model_index.json names the plain Flux2KleinPipeline. Read by NFKMLXReleasedSizesTests.testFlux2Klein9BKVMatchesTheReleasedShapes through IK_SHAPES_ROOT.

Mistral-Small 3.2 24B, the text front end FLUX.2 [dev] conditions on. UNGATED, unlike every FLUX.2 release above klein 4B, so its headers are walked from Mistral AI's own repository (585 tensors across 10 shards, 44.7 GB bf16). 363 of them are the decoder under a `language_model.` prefix; the other 222 are the Pixtral-style vision tower and its connector, which this reads past. The release is `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`, so its decoder sits under `text_config` while the top-level `architectures` names the wrapper. 24 billion parameters are 48 GB at bf16, above what a 32 GB machine holds, so the numeric check is `run_reference.py flux2_text_mistral` at a small configuration of the same shape and this inventory is the structural half. FLUX.2 [dev] bundles its own copy of these weights, so the standalone repository is the architecture reference rather than a download the port needs.

The klein 4B RELEASE itself, not a shape inventory: `transformer/` (7.22 GB), `vae/` (0.16 GB), `text_encoder/` (7.5 GB, two shards) and `tokenizer/`, 15 GB in all, fetched with `curl -4` because `hf download` stalls on this host's IPv6 route. The root `flux-2-klein-4b.safetensors` duplicates `transformer/` and is not fetched. It backs the released-weight measurements `run_reference.py flux2_real` / `flux2_real_f32` (--checkpoint <root>/transformer), `flux2_vae_real` (<root>/vae) and `flux2_text_real` (<root>), read through IK_VAL_FLUX2_KLEIN_4B, IK_VAL_FLUX2_KLEIN_4B_VAE and IK_VAL_FLUX2_KLEIN_4B_ROOT. The text encoder is a Qwen3ForCausalLM that is NOT byte-identical to Qwen/Qwen3-4B (two shards against three, no shard hash in common).

FLUX.2 [klein] BASE 4B transformer, the un-distilled sibling of klein 4B and also ungated. Its config is identical to klein 4B's, so the value of this inventory is that the declared `.klein4B` geometry reads a SECOND release rather than having been fitted to one checkpoint (169 tensors).

FLUX.2's small decoder (62M, ungated): the full encoder at a narrower decoder, `decoder_block_out_channels` [96,192,384,384] against [128,256,512,512]. The first ASYMMETRIC autoencoder here, which is why `NFKMLXSDVAEConfiguration` gained `decoderBlockChannels`. The repository keeps `config.json` AND `diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors` at its ROOT, which is why shapes.py no longer picks the weight name from whether a subfolder was given: it tries the likely name and falls back.

cuts_comment: Releases too large for float32 here, cut to their first N decoder layers by `python3 truncate.py <repo> <out> N`, which fetches only the kept tensors by HTTP range request into compact shards and writes a reduced config.json and index. training_records_comment: The training-objective records a recipe's parity test reads. Each is an oracle output, not a download, so fetch.py neither fetches nor points at it: the record lives at `record`, a path under ~/.inferkit-validation or an absolute one for a record kept on another volume, its key reaches ~/.inferkit-validation.json through the IO Coordinator, and it regenerates with `python3 run_reference.py <command> <record>` under the named oracle environment, with each source variable pointing at the reference the record was measured against.
